title: Stripe Payments vs Stripe Managed Payments
summary: Two modes in the Stripe ecosystem with different legal sellers, responsibilities, eligibility, checkout rules, and total fees.
recommendation: Use ordinary Stripe Payments when you want to remain the merchant and own the operating stack. Consider Managed Payments for eligible digital transactions where transferring indirect-tax, fraud, dispute, and transaction-support responsibility justifies the added fee and preview constraints.

differences.second: Link is presented as Merchant of Record for the managed transaction.
differences.whyItMatters: This is a responsibility change, not a Stripe settings shortcut.

differences.first: Payment-method pricing, such as 2.9% + $0.30 for US domestic cards.
differences.second: Adds 3.5% per successful Managed Payments transaction to Payments fees.
differences.whyItMatters: Compare the combined amount, not 3.5% against 2.9%.

differences.first: Generally available in Stripe-supported business locations.
differences.second: Public preview with a narrower supported-business country list.
differences.whyItMatters: Preview status and eligibility must be procurement gates.

differences.first: Broad eligible online goods and services.
differences.second: Eligible digital products; services, physical goods, platforms, and multiple categories are prohibited.
differences.whyItMatters: Many ordinary Stripe businesses are not eligible for Managed Payments.

differences.first: Your merchant identity and configured Stripe checkout experience.
differences.second: Sold through Link, standardized transaction emails, and Link order support.
differences.whyItMatters: Brand, support, receipts, statements, and customer expectations change.

scenarios.when: You already use Checkout for eligible digital products and want MoR only in selected markets.
scenarios.reason: Transaction-level enablement is its distinctive advantage.

scenarios.when: You need Elements, platforms, physical goods, services, or maximum billing flexibility.
scenarios.reason: Managed Payments eligibility and integration limits are material.

scenarios.when: You are not comfortable depending on preview behavior.
scenarios.reason: Managed Payments remains explicitly documented as public preview.
